newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt funds long but on hold - MCM survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt funds long but on hold - MCM survey.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers maintained a bullish outlook but kept their debt portfolios on hold in the past week pending results of the Presidential election, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
"Most (portfolio managers) said the bond market needs to get past elections and refunding," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
"Maintaining long duration exposure, managers see no reason to extend further ... Want to wait a few weeks," added McTeague.

The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to a modest 106.7 percent in the week ended October 28 from 106.3 percent the prior week. A reading above 100 percent indicates respondents are mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 15 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," up from 12 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" also rose, to 28 percent, from 26 percent in the week ended October 21.
Fifty-seven percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 62 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 2.60 percent, against 2.49 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 20 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, unchanged from the previous week, while 25 percent underweighted it. The remaining 55 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 54 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 15 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 40 domestic participants, who manage about $100 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
